deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is not Riemann's own writing. It is the second page of a letter, almost certainly from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber, written c. 1875/76 during the editing of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The previous page begins 'Lieber Freund!' and the next page continues with Dedekind's (m,n) formula system. The page reports the following.

(1) The 'Richtigkeitsbeweis' (proof of correctness) still missing in his earlier postcard, concerning an identity Σ a_ν/ν = Σ a^0_ν/ν, was found on the afternoon after a day of failed attempts. This belongs to his method, taken from a faint Riemann sheet, applied to the first-order transformation of the theta/eta functions. Read in modern terms, it is part of a proof of the transformation law of log η(ω) under SL2(Z) by comparing coefficient sums of logarithmic series; that reading is mine.

(2) Dedekind wrote this up in about 8–9 folio pages. He added, on letter paper, a sketch of the foundations of a new theory of modular equations, which he had devised some years earlier mainly with complex multiplication in view.

(3) Weber's conjecture is mentioned: Riemann's real aim in the papers was to find examples of trigonometric series. Dedekind did not examine the papers from that angle.

(4) Dedekind wanted to clarify the other Riemann page he had noticed (marked *), and to check Riemann's 'chaotic' formulas. He has fully verified only Riemann's first formula for log k in the first case. For the second formula he found agreement, on one numerical example, between Riemann's final formula and his own formulas. His own formulas come from the properties of the 'merkwürdige Zahlen (m,n)', i.e. Dedekind sums, continued on the next page.

Modern context:
- Riemann's fragment (Werke XXVIII, 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen') gives the behaviour of log k, log k', log(2K/π) as ω approaches a rational m/n.
- Dedekind's commentary on it (Erläuterungen zu den Fragmenten XXVIII, 1876/1892) introduced the transformation formula of log η with the correction term (m,n) = 12 n s(m,n).
- The two properties he cites are (m',n)=(m,n) for m'≡m (mod n), and the reciprocity law m(m,n)+n(n,m)=1+m²+n²−3mn.
errors: No mathematical steps on this page to check. The only formula, Σ a_ν/ν = Σ a^0_ν/ν, is cited without context, so its precise content cannot be verified from this page alone.
Dedekind reports that the second log k formula was checked only on one numerical example, not proved.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter by Dedekind (to Weber) about editing Riemann's Nachlass, with no mathematics by Riemann. Its contents match the published history: Dedekind's commentary on fragment XXVIII and the introduction of Dedekind sums. It adds only biographical colour about the timing of Dedekind's proof.
